chapter: Part Two: theaters and the Chicago scene
title: Head arrangements, Louis Armstrong's ear and Tate's library
summary: Armstrong didn't read but could play overtures; Tate had a huge library.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: When did head arrangements come in, in big bands?
I think they came in -- same time, I think, that Louie and them was with Carroll Dickerson's band at the Sunset.
Would they use a lot of head arrangements?
Yeah, they used a lot of head
arrangements, especially with Louie, you know.
So they had to use head arrangements?
He could play those overtures, though, and I don't understand how he could do that.
I guess he had a heck of an ear.

Yeah, regular overtures. Orpheus in the Underworld,* Poet and Peasant, oh, my goodness, I don't know, anything you could name. But Tate had a library that was, oh, I mean just as great as any of the ballroom Kess orchestras downtown had.
Uh-huh. He'd have to, doing that kind of work.
Yeah, playing pictures, for silent pictures. Because they sent out the cue sheets with the picture. And you had to gear your music to the picture from the cue sheet.
